In the USA, if a copyright infringement case has been decided by the judicial system to be fair use, is it more accurate to say that a) copyright infringement occurred but it was legally excused, or b) copyright infringement did not occur?

message.content: Answer B is more accurate. Fair use makes the use lawful, so no copyright infringement occurred. The Copyright Act states fair use is not infringement. The copying itself may have occurred, but the law does not call it an infringement.
